Sam — thanks for the details and the trace. Quick answers up front:
- Our standard EUR collection account for hosted customers is a EUR nostro held at BigBank London. In many cases BigBank will pass intermediary/cover bank fees back as deductions unless the originating instruction explicitly uses "OUR" (payer covers all fees).
- Redwood does not automatically gross-up intermediary fees for hosted invoices; we historically absorb small correspondent fees for Enterprise Contracts on a case-by-case basis with manager approval.

A few clarifying asks so I can route this correctly to ops:
1) Who initiated the transfer (bank name + sending BIC)? (helps us see whether they used cover or intermediary routing).
2) Was the instruction sent as OUR vs BEN vs SHA? The trace often includes that tag.
3) Is the payee able to accept a revised instruction with an explicit OUR or to receive via an alternate USD account?

If you can share the sending bank and the exact MT103/trace extract I can coordinate with BigBank correspondent support. I will loop in Laura on policy for absorption thresholds.

-Vivek

Hi Sam — looping Marissa (billing disputes) and confirming Redwood's pragmatic approach so we can close this with your AR team.

Policy & proposed resolution:
- For hosted customers (no reserved contract), we typically do NOT gross-up for correspondent bank charges; those are treated as bank-level intermediary deductions and are passed to the beneficiary.
- For Enterprise customers (contracted revenue) we will consider absorbing up to a fixed operational tolerance to avoid disrupting customer relationships — typically up to USD 50 per event, subject to manager sign-off and one-off credit if needed.

Given GlobalHealth's ARR and payment frequency, propose the following:
1) For this incident, Redwood will absorb the EUR 38.47 (convert to USD at today's spot) and issue a one-time credit to the payee's next invoice — no chargeback. I will coordinate with Marissa on the credit memo.
2) Going forward, please ask payers to instruct their banks to send payments as "OUR" when the payer agrees to cover all intermediary fees, or alternatively send USD via the payee's USD account (details below).

Revised wiring options for GlobalHealth to pass to their bank:
- Option A (payer covers fees): Instruct sending bank: Payment Type: OUR; Beneficiary: Redwood Inference US LLC; Account: 12345678; Bank: Redwood Nostro - BigBank NY (BIC: BBNKUS33); Reference: INV-202704-789
- Option B (payee receives net): Send to EUR collection account (no change) but be aware intermediary fees may apply.

Marissa — please prepare a credit memo for ~EUR 38.47 (or USD equivalent) against INV-202704-789 and mark as "intermediary charge concession" against the invoice and mark as "intermediary charge concession".
